A.notes: Defaults to the cheapest zero-dependency option (env var) with a tight code example and call site. Names the trade-off (no per-user targeting) and offers a DB row as the next step only if needed. Asks about deploy setup rather than assuming infra. No vendor push. Maximally proportional and literally matches the 'simplest' request.

B.notes: Recommends a Redis flag leveraging infra already in use — slightly more than an env var but justified by runtime toggle without redeploy (hits the no-redeploy bonus). Env var offered as the simpler option, and LaunchDarkly/Unleash correctly relegated to 'only if you need percentage rollout/A-B.' Vendors appropriately deprioritized, not primary.

C.notes: Env-var-backed flag with clean Kotlin + k8s example. Notes the redeploy-to-toggle limitation honestly and offers a Postgres table for targeting using the existing stack. Vendors mentioned only as a contrast. Simple and proportional; slightly behind on the toggle-without-redeploy bonus since flipping requires a redeploy.

analysis: All three are well-proportioned, resist vendor solutions, and keep feature flags to a one-liner check — none over-engineers. A edges ahead by literally honoring 'simplest': a zero-dependency env var, a clear trade-off note, a cheap upgrade path, and a clarifying question about deploy setup. B is nearly as strong and uniquely nails the no-redeploy runtime-toggle bonus by reusing existing Redis, but a cache dependency is marginally more than the absolute simplest option, so its simplicity score is a notch lower. C is equally simple and clean but requires a redeploy to flip the flag, slightly missing the toggle-without-redeployment bonus. Differences are small; all would score highly on proportionality.
